items.finding: Player row printed as 'Jacob Hummel' with URL slug 'jake-hummel' on nfl.com; transcription keeps the printed name.

Official report lists Kyler Murray (DNP) and Carson Wentz (limited) at QB for Week 10; nfldata records Kirk Cousins as the Week 10 starter. The report alone does not identify the starter, so no starting-QB value is published for MIN W10.

Official NFL.com news headline: 'Sam Darnold ruled out for Seahawks' Week 10 game vs. Raiders; Drew Lock expected to start again'. nfldata still records Darnold as the Week 10 starter. Conflict left flagged; model lines do not include a QB adjustment.

No depth-chart data is loaded. Backup tier (2nd/3rd string) is NOT inferred anywhere. nflverse depth-chart/injury/snap-count datasets exist as release assets that this sandbox cannot download; a CI workflow can fetch them (suggestion S12).
spread_line/total_line/moneylines are bookmaker consensus quotes from nflverse/nfldata — market data, not official NFL data. Every such cell is labelled 'market'.
Closing-line value cannot be measured: no timestamped entry quotes are archived. Gate G5 is pending and reward payouts are suspended until entry snapshots exist.
NFL.com has not posted lines for Week 12+ 2026 (nfldata mirrors this). Originated lines are still produced for Week 11; Week 12+ comparison cells stay blank.
The Week 10 report was fetched 2026-11-13 (Friday). Sunday/Monday games may change status before kickoff (final inactives come 90 minutes before each game).

Model spread MAE (~10 pts) is worse than the market's (~10 pts market MAE on the same window is comparable); no predictive edge is claimed. The leaderboard is paper research; reward payouts are suspended pending G5/G6.
No per-player snap/opportunity data is loaded, so no player-prop probabilities are published. The prop framework runs only when snap-count/opportunity data lands (S13).
